newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica seeks U.S. ally to conquer Latam market.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica seeks U.S. ally to conquer Latam market.

text.p: Telefonica Internacional, the international arm of Spanish telecommunications group Telefonica, said Monday it was considering linking up with a U.S. company to offer global services in Latin America.

"We are choosing between the four or five U.S. operators the one which we consider best to develop our pan-American project," Marcial Portela, managing director of Telefonica Internacional (TISA), said in an interview.

The pan-American network is an ambitious project with which TISA plans to link all the countries where it is established in Latin America -- Argentina, Chile, Peru, Venezuela, Colombia and Mexico -- to Europe and the United States via underwater cables.
"It is a mature project which will be put into action at the end of this year, because now we are waiting to see if we do it by ourselves or together with a U.S. ally," Portela said.
The network would connect Telefonica's international services and act as a carrier for other telecommunications firms.
"The cost is very low because the cables and the clients are already there," he said, pointing out the high potential of the telecommunications sector in Latin America.

Linking up with a U.S. telecommunications operator would also allow Telefonica to enter the U.S. market, where it has taken its first tentative steps through its Puerto Rican subsidiary Telefonica Larga Distancia.

"We are going to make some pilot investments to find out if being a Latin American operator gives us any comparative advantage with the Spanish-speaking market in the U.S.," said the managing director.
In the next three months, TISA will launch a long-distance calling card on the U.S. market.

But the Spanish operator was not interested in any foreign telecommunications firm buying into its capital, Portela said. U.S. giants AT&T Corp. and GTE Corp. had been rumoured as potential shareholders in Telefonica Internacional.

"We do not want another operator in Telefonica's capital because we believe they would not contribute anything and besides it may become complicated if their interests are different from ours," Portela said.
TISA will not increase its stake in Venezuela's CANTV when it is privatised in mid-November and will focus on Chile, Peru and countries in the Mercosur trade alliance instead.

"As a matter of routine, we will have a look at other business opportunities in privatisations next year, but without the strength or the ambition that we want to put in the Mercosur projects," Portela said.
The Mercosur alliance groups Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay.
In particular, TISA will focus on the privatisation of Brazil's Companhia Riograndense de Telecomunicacoes (CRT) in November, having qualified to bid for the 35-percent stake on offer.
If it fails to win the auction, TISA will study participating in the Brazilian cellular phone market and will prepare for the privatisation of Brazil's state telecoms monopoly Telebras.
